review_argument.evidence_grade_statement: Clinical associations (antibiotics, metabolite correlations) are observational (Grade C); FMT and engineered bacteria interventions are Phase I/II only (Grade B); no Phase III RCT evidence exists (Grade insufficient for clinical recommendation).
supporting_lines: Observational data consistently links post-ICI antibiotic exposure to reduced survival (HR 1.27 in 21,108-patient cohort), with tumor-type specificity suggesting differential microbiome dependency.
Phase II FMT trials demonstrate promising efficacy signals (ORR 70-80%) but reveal regimen-dependent safety risks (65% grade ≥3 AEs in dual-ICI melanoma), indicating intervention complexity.
Metabolite mechanisms (inosine-UBA6, SCFA-HDAC) have preclinical validation and human biomarker correlations, but lack direct human TME concentration measurements needed for therapeutic targeting.
The field currently lacks Phase III RCT confirmation of reproducible survival benefit from microbiome interventions, limiting clinical readiness despite mechanistic plausibility.
review_argument.thesis: The gut microbiome modulates ICI efficacy in solid tumours through immune, metabolic, and barrier-mediated mechanisms, but clinical translation remains constrained by the absence of Phase III randomized trial evidence and limited human metabolite quantification data.

shared_scope.central_question: How does the gut microbiome modulate the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in solid tumours, and what mechanisms mediate that effect?
shared_scope.provisional_scope: This review synthesizes evidence on the role of the gut microbiome in modulating immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) efficacy across solid tumours. It covers clinical associations (antibiotic exposure timing, FMT outcomes), microbial signatures (taxa, metabolites), mechanistic pathways (immune modulation, metabolic signaling, barrier integrity), and therapeutic interventions. The scope excludes hematological malignancies unless mechanistic insights are directly transferable to solid tumours. Emphasis is placed on human clinical data over preclinical models, with explicit notation of evidence grades (observational vs. interventional).
shared_scope.review_title: Gut Microbiome Modulation of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Efficacy in Solid Tumours: Mechanisms and Clinical Evidence
scope_adjustments_from_supplements: Explicitly state that no completed Phase III randomized controlled trials of microbiome interventions in ICI-treated solid tumour patients exist as of late 2025; current evidence relies on Phase I/II trials and observational data.

Acknowledge that human tumour microenvironment metabolite concentrations (inosine, SCFAs) are not directly quantified in available studies; plasma stratification data and proxy biomarkers (UBA6 expression) are used instead.
Distinguish tumor-type specificity in antibiotic sensitivity (head/neck, RCC, breast show stronger post-ICI antibiotic effects; lung, melanoma show weaker associations in large cohort data).
Note that FMT Phase II data shows promising ORR (70-80% in NSCLC/melanoma) but elevated irAE rates in dual-ICI contexts (65% grade ≥3 AEs in melanoma cohort).

source_selection_principles: Prioritize human clinical data for efficacy claims; use preclinical data primarily for mechanistic explanation with explicit species notation.
Distinguish observational associations (antibiotics, metabolite stratification) from interventional data (FMT trials) when discussing efficacy.
Exclude studies focused solely on hematological malignancies unless mechanistic insights are explicitly linked to solid tumour pathways.
Flag studies lacking adjustment for clinical confounders (infection severity, performance status) when citing antibiotic effects.
Do not generalize metabolite effects without specifying context (ICI type, concentration proxy, tumor type).
When Phase III RCT data is absent, cite review sources confirming the gap rather than implying search failure.
Retain original study limitations (sample size, stratification vs. absolute concentrations) in all mechanistic claims.

unresolved_limits.description: No completed Phase III randomized controlled trials of microbiome interventions in ICI-treated solid tumour patients with published primary efficacy outcomes (OS/PFS/ORR) exist as of late 2025.
unresolved_limits.impact_on_conclusions: Cannot recommend microbiome interventions as standard care; must frame FMT and engineered bacteria as investigational.

unresolved_limits.source_confirmation: CorpusId:252309032 and related searches confirm plasma stratification only; human TME tissue concentrations not measured.
